newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya Commercial Bank lifts Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Kenya Commercial Bank lifts Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: Foreign demand for Kenya Commercial Bank on Tuesday pushed the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index up by 20.67 points to stand at 3091.71, brokers and bourse officials said.
Turnover was posted at 18.597 million shillings traded on 440,903 shares from 14.630 million shillings traded on 283,130 shares on Monday.
Bourse officials said there was overbidding for KCB stock which caused the share to jump to 83.50 from 79. Foreign investors bought 129,000 KCB shares at between 73.50 and 84.

"Foreigners are extremely interested in our market because they believe it is one of the most lucrative emerging markets," a senior broker said. "In fact, the problem we have is that we don't have adequate supply to match the demand."
Brokers predicted that there would be enough demand for Kenya Commercial Bank to sustain its upward price movement.
Sasini Tea and Coffee traded 4,092 shares at 60.50, while Rea Vipingo traded at 10.50 unchanged.
There was good trading activity on the financials board which brokers attributed to investors anticipating good year-end results sometime this month and early next year.
Credit Finance Bank traded 126,585 shares at 18.85 from 18.90 while Standard Chartered Bank traded at 47 from 46.50.
Kenya Oil Co, suspended in May after deciding to delist, resumed trading at the NSE on Tuesday. Its delisting proposal was rejected by the NSE. It dealt 634 shares at 50.
East African Development Bank corporate bonds, trading at the Nairobi bourse since December 9, were officially launched.
Three deals worth five million shillings were transacted at between 101.29 and 101.79 percent.
